**Finding submitted: deviation (WARRANTY).**

**What I found**

- **Section 9 "TRUELINK WARRANTIES" (p0059–p0060)** is the only TrueLink-side warranty in the document, and it covers *only* Y2K date processing. There is no professional/workmanlike services warranty, no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the Interface or related software, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no remedy.
- **Section 8 (p0051, p0055–p0056)** imposes exactly those warranties on *Client* — compliance with laws, IP non-infringement, and freedom from viruses/worms/Trojan horses. The warranty burden is one-directional against us, confirming the planner's hint.
- **Section 12 (p0076)** disclaims implied warranties of merchantability and fitness. The "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT" carve-out is correctly worded, so no separate carve-out edit was needed — but with no express performance warranty to carve out, the practical effect approaches the walk-away "AS IS" outcome.
- Searches for "AS IS" and "workmanlike" returned nothing; p0042 adds a further TrueLink disclaimer for credit data accuracy.

**Why deviation rather than missing:** a TrueLink warranty section exists, but it fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) on every material term.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** inserted a new paragraph after p0060 at the **preferred** position — professional and workmanlike Hosting/Support Services, 12-month conformance warranty for the Interface and related software, compliance with laws, no malicious code, and a re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy at TrueLink's option. Drafting deliberately reuses the document's own defined terms (Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, compensation) and mirrors the malicious-code language already imposed on Client in p0056, which should make it hard to resist as unreasonable. The comment offers the 90/30-day fallback as a landing zone.

One judgment call worth flagging for you: I went to the preferred 12-month software period even though the seed precedent sits at fallback, on the reasoning that the Agreement's initial term is 1 year (p0078) so a 12-month warranty matches the term. If you would rather open at 90 days to conserve negotiating capital, that is a one-number change to the proposal.
